A patient with a history of papillary thyroid carcinoma presents for a surveillance ultrasound. The sonographer identifies a 1.5 cm oval-shaped lymph node in the right jugulodigastric region. On grayscale imaging, the node is hypoechoic and lacks a visible fatty hilum. Color Doppler demonstrates peripheral vascularity. Which of the following features is most concerning for metastatic involvement in this lymph node?

During ultrasound-guided fine needle aspiration (FNA) of a suspicious thyroid nodule, the sonographer observes the needle tip within the nodule, but the patient suddenly coughs and the needle moves. What is the immediate next step the sonographer should take to ensure patient safety and procedure efficacy?

A 45-year-old female presents for a thyroid ultrasound due to a palpable neck mass. The sonographer identifies a 1.8 cm solid, hypoechoic nodule with microcalcifications and irregular margins in the right thyroid lobe. There is also evidence of extracapsular extension. Based on these findings, what is the most appropriate TIRADS category?

A 58-year-old male undergoes a thyroid ultrasound which reveals a 0.7 cm, predominantly cystic nodule with a few peripheral punctate echogenic foci. The nodule is isoechoic to the adjacent thyroid tissue. What TIRADS category would most likely be assigned to this nodule based on these features?

During a follow-up thyroid ultrasound for a known nodule, the sonographer observes a 1.2 cm hypoechoic, oval-shaped lesion posterior to the mid-pole of the left thyroid lobe. The lesion demonstrates internal vascularity on color Doppler and has a more homogeneous echotexture compared to the adjacent thyroid parenchyma. The patient's serum calcium levels are elevated. What is the most likely identity of this lesion?

A sonographer is attempting to visualize a small, deep lesion in the liver. Which of the following transducer frequencies would provide the best balance between penetration and axial resolution for this scenario?

A sonographer is performing a vascular study and notices spectral broadening in the Doppler waveform despite optimizing the sample volume and angle. Which of the following transducer characteristics would most likely contribute to this artifact?

During an abdominal ultrasound, the sonographer observes a hypoechoic area posterior to a highly reflective gallstone that appears anechoic. This phenomenon is known as acoustic shadowing. Which of the following physics principles best explains this artifact?

When performing a color Doppler evaluation of renal artery stenosis, the sonographer notices color aliasing in the stenotic segment. To resolve this, which of the following adjustments would be most appropriate?

A sonographer is performing a musculoskeletal ultrasound and observes an artifact that makes a tendon appear thicker than it truly is due to the sound beam striking it at an oblique angle. What is this artifact called?
